response.title: Can I leave my refrigerator plugged into a power station all the time so it switches over automatically when the power goes out?
response.answer:
Yes! You can leave your refrigerator plugged into a portable power station 24/7 and have it automatically switch to battery power during an outage. However, you need a power station that supports UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) or EPS (Emergency Power Supply) functionality.

Not every power station supports this.

How it works

Under normal conditions, the station supplies power to your refrigerator from the wall, using either AC pass-through or an internal transfer system, depending on the model.

When the power goes out, it switches to its battery and inverter automatically. When utility power returns, it switches back and recharges.

Four things to check before buying

UPS/EPS capability: Look for automatic switchover. Some models switch in 10–30 milliseconds, which is usually fine for a conventional refrigerator, though not guaranteed for every model.

Continuous operation: The manufacturer must explicitly support leaving AC input and output connected continuously. Some stations have timeouts or operating restrictions.

Compressor startup power: Your refrigerator might consume 100–250 watts while running but briefly require much more when the compressor starts. The station must handle that surge.

Battery capacity: A 1,000 Wh power station might run a typical refrigerator for roughly 6–12 hours, depending on actual consumption, temperature, and inverter losses.

One important consideration

Not all power stations are ideal for permanent UPS use. Some continuously run their inverter, increasing electricity consumption, fan noise, and battery wear. Others offer efficient AC bypass and battery charge limits, making them better suited to 24/7 operation.

For a refrigerator, I would prioritize a model with AC bypass, automatic transfer, a pure sine wave inverter, and a LiFePO4 battery.

Also, keep the power station in a dry, ventilated location, and plug it directly into a properly grounded wall outlet according to the manufacturer's instructions.

I have two questions

Which power station do you have or plan to buy? (EcoFlow, Bluetti, Jackery, Anker, etc.)

Is your refrigerator a full-size kitchen refrigerator or a smaller mini-fridge?

I can help determine whether that exact setup is safe for continuous use, whether switchover will work, and approximately how long the refrigerator will run during an outage.
